order.why: Connect a son’s arrival with his father’s work.
shortened: O spiritual friends! Jinab-i-Abu'l-Hasan (upon him be the Glory of God) traversed a great distance and crossed vast deserts and passed over seas until he reached the shore of the Blessed Spot. At the Sacred Threshold he engaged in the work and service of his respected father.

order.why: Remember a life of tending the gardens.
shortened: For some time he dwelt near the luminous Shrine, that verdant garden, the gathering-place of the Concourse on High, circumambulating the illumined resting-place and tending the sacred gardens.

order.why: Give the work of gardening an individual name.
shortened: O handmaiden of God! Jinab-i-Jamshid is with us and is occupied as gardener in the Garden of Paradise, which for several years was the place honored by the presence of the Blessed Beauty.

order.why: Keep the account of labor and loss in the garden.
shortened: The Covenant-breakers had also taken the garden of the shrine from us, even though I and the friends had hauled the soil and planted flowers with our own hands.
Twenty fakhuras - we bought this house just for the Blessed Beauty's room and planted trees along both sides of the path.

order.why: Attend to the ordinary difficulties of tending trees.
Let planting flowers become a shared devotional act.
shortened: With unsurpassed humility and fervour, and in a spirit of perfect reverence and devotion, ye have hastened unto the Habitation of Holiness, and in those sacred precincts embosoming the inestimable Gift - the Centre around which circle in adoration the Concourse on high; the Luminous Sepulchre; the Hallowed Spot - ye have with your own hands planted fragrant blossoms.

order.why: Join song and longing to the imagery of a watered garden.
shortened: Thou wert present at the Threshold of Oneness, drank from the cup of grace, perfumed thy nostrils with the holy fragrances of the Blessed Spot, illumined thy face with the dust of God's threshold, and with melody, song, chanting, ecstasy, attraction and rapture watered the rose-garden and flower-bed of the Sacred Valley.

order.why: Join visitation with watering.
shortened: You made the dust of the blessed threshold the kohl of your eyes and watered and irrigated the illumined garden.

order.why: Make service itself a source of light.
shortened: O you who circle round the gathering place of the Supreme Concourse! Praise be to God that through grace and bounty you were enabled to prostrate yourself at the Sacred Threshold, to press your forehead to the perfumed dust of the Holy Court, and to illumine your countenance with the light of servitude and the watering at the Purified Garden.

order.why: Honor the deputy who carries water.
shortened: Jinab-i-Aqa Mihdi, you are my deputy in watering the Blessed Shrine. Every drop of that water is the water of life itself and the cause of life in the hearts of those who prostrate themselves. This servant is the caretaker of that sacred soil and the one who waters that blessed garden.

order.why: Carry water on behalf of an absent friend.
shortened: In the Holy Garden of the Sacred Threshold we have been and are engaged in remembrance and prayer for you. You have not been and will not be forgotten. A jug of water was carried on behalf of you and used to water the garden of the Holy Shrine.

order.why: Extend such representation to the friends of Egypt.
Bring flowers and prayer together.
Let travel culminate in serving water to others.
Preserve a donor’s candelabrum as a sign of service.
shortened: Since thy manner, deed, spirit and efforts have brought me such deep delight, I have sent the candelabrum you donated to the Sacred Shrine so that a sign from you may be preserved at that Blessed Threshold.

order.why: Retain a vase as a remembrance of a journey.
shortened: O beloved of 'Abdu'l-Baha! At this moment, near the Holy Shrine, I have taken in my own hands the vase which you had sent as a memento of my journey to America, and placed it in the Holy Shrine.

order.why: Include the practical request for carpets.
Pray that nearby residents become channels of grace.
shortened: O my Lord! Make those who dwell near Thy Sacred House channels for the water of Thy grace that descends from the clouds of bounty and generosity. Then make them servants at Thy sacred threshold of exalted station, strivers to uplift its perfumed pillars, and those who bow down upon its amber-scented earth.

order.why: Return to a night’s joy in the Shrine’s vicinity.
Consider prayer at places associated with God.
Let the spring flowers accompany the reported gratitude.
Retain the speaker’s praise of the city and its future.
shortened: Truly thou art the mother of all the cities of the world and thou art blessed beyond the grasp of human imagination! Thy spiritual station is very great and thy fame shall reach to the uttermost parts of the earth!'

order.why: Keep the vision of surrounding gardens in its reported form.
shortened: This is the Blessed house, do you realise it is the Blessed House of Baha'u'llah. All that quarter in which the House is situated will be destroyed and will be transformed into wonderful Parks and gardens. It will become most heavenly.

order.why: Imagine future pilgrims arriving with flowers.
Let rocky ground become a place visited by many peoples.
shortened: The rocky crags of this mountain shall be transformed into gardens of flowers and roses, and shall become a place of pilgrimage for all the peoples of the world.

order.why: Make shade and a walkable avenue part of hospitality.
Include places of rest along the pilgrims’ path.
shortened: On foot and bareheaded, and with humility and modesty, and in a state of supplication and entreaty, chanting divine verses and prayers, they will attain to a visit of the Shrine of the Exalted One [the Bab]. On the path to the Shrine of the Exalted One, there will be pools of water, gardens and places for rest and respite.
Afterwards, with bouquets of flowers over their shoulders, and while reciting divine verses and prayers, they will visit the Shrine of Baha'u'llah.

order.why: Open the shrine’s gates to all in prayer.
shortened: These are servants of Thine who live in Thy sanctified city, in the vicinity of Thy Holy Shrine - a Shrine whose gates are open unto all.

order.why: Connect the reported understanding of the Shrine with worship.
shortened: Miss Boylan said Abdul-Baha replied that he had fulfilled that prophecy by building the Tomb of the Bab. He said the Tomb of the Bab on Mount Carmel was the first Mashrekol-Azkar, and that Temple is already built.

order.why: Leave room for worship or education in an endowed plot.
Close with the reported vision of sacred remembrance joined to hospitals, schools and refuge.

questions: How do the passages about lamps, dust, memory, and spirit change your understanding of what makes a place holy?
What forms of care emerge from reverence, and how do preserving a house, carrying stones, and tending a garden express different responsibilities?
How might the accounts of inward turning from afar and remembrance on behalf of others enlarge the meaning of pilgrimage?
How would you distinguish the collection’s prayers, symbolic descriptions, practical instructions, and reported historical claims when reading them together?
What does Jacob’s recognition at Bethel illuminate about sacred memory, and what differences remain between that narrative and these accounts of shrines and pilgrimage?
How can love for a particular sacred place encourage hospitality, attention to suffering elsewhere, and service through the neighboring institutions of worship and education?

references.label: 1 · Genesis 28:10–22 · Jacob awakens at Bethel
references.note: Jacob’s ordinary stopping place becomes the site of a dream, a divine promise, a marked stone, and a vow. Compare recognition and remembrance here with the readings on material traces and spiritual attention. Preserve the narrative’s particular covenantal setting while asking how an encounter changes a person’s relationship to a place.
